source_review.notes: Checked the primary MapReduce, Google File System, delay-scheduling, Snowflake, and Borg papers plus current official HDFS, Spark, and Kubernetes documentation. All ten referenced URLs returned HTTP 200 on the retrieval date after selecting the authors' reachable MIT-hosted delay-scheduling copy.

evidence: Reviewed task, candidate resource, input copy, version, topology path, availability, startup, compute, transfer, output, byte-weighted locality, amplification, and cache-reuse notation.
Checked feasibility is applied before cost comparison and that time, byte, rate, and ratio dimensions remain compatible.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The model distinguishes authoritative objects, replicas, caches, transient intermediates, topology, queue state, and policy constraints.

evidence: Executed locality-scheduling-comparison with Python 3.14.4 and reproduced round-robin 3,000 remote MB with 15.67-second makespan and locality-aware 1,200 remote MB with 12.00-second makespan.
Recomputed the 60.00% remote-byte reduction, the 3.67-second fixture difference, exercise completion estimates 6.5 and 8 seconds, and byte locality 900/10,900=8.26%.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Fixture arithmetic is exact under fixed rates and sequential assignment; it is neither an optimality proof nor a production benchmark.

evidence: Re-derived the candidate finish estimate as availability plus startup, compute/local I/O, required transfers, output, and modeled contention.
Checked the bounded-wait comparison in which locality delay is justified only when avoided remote cost exceeds waiting and opportunity cost within fairness and deadline constraints.
Derived request-count versus byte-weighted locality and reusable-staging conditions without promoting estimates to guarantees.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Locality, feasibility, critical-path completion, fairness, reliability, and monetary cost remain distinct objectives.

evidence: Reviewed missing and stale location hints, wrong object versions, zero locality preference, short tasks, long queues, hot data, remote accelerators, NUMA distance, cold caches, low reuse, cache eviction, expanded broadcast size, and saturated links.

Reviewed worker, cache, device, rack, zone, region, metadata, and network failure; retry storms; speculation; topology mislabeling; autoscaling churn; residency; offline clinical devices; and rollback.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Cold/warm, steady/failure, single/mixed-tenant, and preference/constraint cases are separately addressed.

evidence: Traced exact input identity and freshness, feasible placement, failure-domain separation, epoch-compatible ownership, cache recoverability, bounded fallback, and unchanged data semantics throughout the chapter.
Checked that all traffic categories, graph edges, critical-path effects, weighted locality measures, and recovery dependencies are included in the evidence obligations.
invariant_checking.notes: Local scheduling is never treated as permission to weaken replica independence, residency, consistency, or recovery.

evidence: Reviewed all seven locality obligations from object identity through retained evidence.

Checked counterexamples for local-equals-fast, same-node-equals-no-movement, strict-affinity progress, task-percentage sufficiency, cache-equals-replica, source-only residency, and per-task optimization.
Reviewed graph-wide movement, replica placement, disaggregated-storage, bounded delay, failure, and fallback arguments.
proof_review.notes: The chapter separates heuristic placement quality, modeled completion, observed fixture behavior, and end-to-end correctness.

evidence: Audited uses of local, feasible, faster, rational, favorable, optimum, safe, durable, authoritative, and critical path.
Confirmed all completion equations and staging comparisons are labeled as estimates with omitted uncertainty and contention identified.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No greedy assignment, locality level, or cache observation is presented as a universal optimality or reliability theorem.

evidence: Reviewed current-system documentation claims, retrieval dates, executable fixture scope, non-benchmark disclaimer, cold/warm measurement requirements, and high-consequence review disclaimer.
Confirmed no production, performance, fairness, availability, clinical-safety, certification, or external-review claim is made.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Production policy requires representative workload, topology, contention, failure, cost, and mixed-tenant evidence.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed locality as a time-varying relation spanning object identity, topology, candidate compute, queue state, transfer, cache, graph edges, failure domains, and policy.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed topology metadata, delay fallback, task and byte metrics, transfer categories, cache lifecycle, replica choice, affinity and anti-affinity, disaggregated storage, autoscaling, observability, incident behavior, and durable recovery. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from locality levels through scheduling and graph-wide trade-offs; ten worked examples and five complete answers cover calculation, diagnosis, policy, architecture comparison, and unfamiliar clinical transfer.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic, cluster-scheduling practitioner, storage vendor, clinical, safety, or certification review is claimed.
